what_happened.line: The board voted to recommend the town not use its right of first refusal to buy a chapter-land parcel on Northfield Road, citing the borrowing that purchase would require.
The board finalized roll-back tax paperwork for several properties leaving forestry or agricultural classification ahead of sale.
An inquiry about a PILOT agreement tied to a proposed battery storage facility was referred to the Select Board and Town Manager rather than handled by the assessors.
The board tentatively set its next full meetings and closed the session by moving into executive session under the state's abatement-confidentiality statute.

why_it_matters: Passing on the first-refusal purchase avoids the town borrowing to buy the Northfield Road property, but clears the way for that land to leave chapter-land status and be sold to a private buyer.

Any PILOT agreement for the battery storage project, which would set what that facility pays the town in lieu of taxes, will now be negotiated by the Select Board, not the assessors -- residents should follow that board for the terms.
Roll-back taxes and betterment billing tied to specific parcels continue moving through the assessors' office and affect the tax bills on those properties.
watch_next: Select Board's handling of the Cycle Electric battery-storage PILOT request
Board of Assessors' next full meeting, tentatively set for March 11

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the shape of the meeting (minutes review, abatement status, the Northfield Road ROFR item, sewer billing discussion, Cycle Electric contact, FY27 growth estimate, and the postponed/upcoming items) but diverge sharply on detail: ours carries dollar figures (roll-back tax amounts, sewer betterment numbers, exemption limits) the official minutes never states, while the official minutes carries whole blocks — abatement counts, executive-session results, the Neighborhood Review Project, the Eagle House presentation date — that our recording-based minutes never captured. The one thing a reader should check first is the ROFR vote: official records it unanimous (3 ayes) while ours heard only two audible ayes plus a prior stated intent to abstain from one member.
